# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 9
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 9

---

*[Hell-Tour: the unrighteous; those who made worldly music to entice souls; the wealthy without pity; the sexually immoral; blasphemers; the outer darkness.]*

1. I beheld a great river of fire in which a multitude of men and women were submerged up to their chins.

2. I asked: "Who are these?"

3. The angel answered: "These are those who had no righteousness in their hearts but worked iniquity instead."

4. Near by I saw another river of fire, and in it women were submerged up to their necks, gnashing their teeth and weeping greatly.

5. The angel said: "These are those who made music for the pleasures of the world and thereby enticed souls to destruction."

6. I saw men and women covered in dust, with filthy garments, cast into darkness, weeping bitterly.

7. The angel said: "These had riches in this world and put their trust in them, and had no pity on orphans and widows, but despised the commandments of God."

8. I beheld another great lake filled with discharging filth and blood, with men and women sunk in it up to their lips.

9. I asked: "Who are these?"

10. The angel answered: "These are those who gave themselves over to fornication."

11. I saw men suspended over the water by their tongues, with fire burning beneath them; they hung in the air.

12. I asked: "Who are these?"

13. The angel answered: "These are those who blasphemed the way of righteousness and said, 'Let us eat and drink and be merry, for tomorrow we die.'"

14. I also saw a lake of fire burning and boiling, in which were men of a pale color. I beheld them.

15. I asked: "What is this lake?" The angel answered: "This is the outer darkness."

---
*LOGOS note: "Outer darkness" (v.15) — the same phrase used in Matthew's parables (8:12, 22:13, 25:30). The APE is drawing directly on dominical tradition. "Music for the pleasures of the world" (v.5) targets entertainers who serve sensuality — a distinctive and unusual category.*
